newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tax inspectors say they raid Murdoch Israel firm.
newsitem.headline: Tax inspectors say they raid Murdoch Israel firm.

text.p: Israeli tax authorities said on Sunday they had raided the offices of a company controlled by media magnate Rupert Murdoch and removed documents but they denied media reports of any arrests.
"It is correct that we are directing an investigation against News Datacom Research," said Sarit Giladi-Dor, a spokeswoman for the Income Tax Authority.

She said details could not be released until the investigation was formally declared public. She denied Israel Radio reports that the authority had petitioned the Jerusalem District Court to detain Murdoch if he were to enter Israel or that there had been any arrests.

The radio said authorities were investigating suspicions that News Datacom Research Ltd, a Jerusalem-based company controlled by Murdoch's UK-based News Corp, had failed to pay as much as 500 million shekels ($153 million) in taxes and royalties owed the Israeli government.
A spokesman for News Datacom said an announcement concerning the investigation would be made at 1300 GMT.
News DataCom develops and sells encryption systems mainly for pay-television broadcasters, like Murdoch's SKY Television.
Giladi-Dor said investigators had also raided the offices of News Datacom's attorneys and auditors.

But she would not comment on an Israel Radio report that authorities suspect the company failed to pay full income tax or royalties due the government in exchange for research and development assistance.
